Key readouts include studies involving cholesterol-lowering drug laroprovstat, Farxiga combinations, Datroway, puxi-sam, camizestrant and saruparib. JPMorgan also highlighted the AVANZAR trial of Datroway, where the readout has moved to the first quarter of 2027 from the fourth quarter of 2026 because progression-free survival events have not yet accumulated. The broker said its analysis of the trial's statistical hurdles suggests the delay could increase confidence in the probability of success, particularly in patients with the TROP2 biomarker. JPMorgan considered whether stronger performance from the control arm or higher levels of censoring could explain the extended trial duration. It concluded that the established KEYNOTE-189 control regimen would need to outperform substantially to fully explain the delay under conservative assumptions. The broker said this supports a more constructive view of the AVANZAR outcome despite limited current market expectations for Datroway. AstraZeneca trades on around 15 times 2027 earnings, broadly in line with the European pharmaceutical sector. JPMorgan said this valuation looks attractive given expected core earnings growth of around 10% between 2027 and 2030, roughly 40% ahead of the sector.

JPMorgan Chase Says That Bitcoin Will Outperform Stocks, Bonds, and Gold Over the Next 10 Years. Here's Why It Might Be Right

It expects the crypto to return 10% annually during that period, versus 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 5.6% f...

Per a new report, the asset management arm of JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) has a base case in which Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) beats domestic stocks, bonds, and even gold during the next 10 years. It expects the crypto to return 10% annually during that period, versus 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 5.6% for broad U.S. bonds, and 5.5% for gold. It's the first time the report has put a range on Bitcoin's returns, and it comes with a handful of heavy caveats. Although the figures it calculated are unlikely to prove true in 2036, the drivers for those results are hard to argue against, and it's my view that JPMorgan Chase is directionally correct. Here's why. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » The JPMorgan Chase report is largely about the investing implications of the macroeconomic conditions facing the world during the coming years, touching on everything from inflation to global warming and, of course, Bitcoin. It expects artificial-intelligence-driven productivity gains to push the U.S. economy's real growth rate to 2.1% annually, with inflation averaging 2.4% in the same period. It also raised its expected annual return for large companies, such as those in the S&P 500 index, from 6.7% to 7.5%, citing strong profit margins. But it contends that Bitcoin will be buoyed by three different factors that will offer better performance than this. The most important driver, with a 65% weight in the calculation, is Bitcoin's slowing supply growth relative to global money growth. The second-most-important factor, with a weight of 30%, is Bitcoin's inclusion in portfolios alongside allocations to other scarce store-of-value assets, such as gold. The last driver is the weakest: the coin's increasing network activity. The bank's estimated growth rate for its base case implies that Bitcoin would be priced at about $211,130 by 2036. Its bear case, which calls for an 11.2% annual loss, implies a price of about $24,817, roughly 70% below its $81,300 level as of Oct. 26. The bull case would see it grow by 16.6% annually. But no matter which of those scenarios plays out, the bank expects the coin's volatility to be 55%, based on historical data. Overall, JPMorgan Chase's projections for Bitcoin's price growth are on the bearish side compared to Bitcoin's history, but they look reasonable. The coin has a 10-year compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 63%.

JPMorgan's CEO just sent a memo to anyone watching the U.S. economy

No summary available

JPMorgan Chase recently delivered another big quarter. The bank earned $15.3 billion, or $5.57 a share, in the third quarter, though the results fell short of Wall Street's estimates in a rare miss, CNBC reported. Revenue still climbed 8% from a year earlier. Yet the more telling part of the repor...

JPMorgan Chase recently delivered another big quarter. The bank earned $15.3 billion, or $5.57 a share, in the third quarter, though the results fell short of Wall Street's estimates in a rare miss, CNBC reported. Revenue still climbed 8% from a year earlier. Yet the more telling part of the report sat beneath the profit. Jamie Dimon used it to flag a short list of risks building under a still-strong economy. In an interview days later, he described the U.S. economy as booming, while warning that inflationary events could still push prices higher. Dimon named them in one sentence: large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates, and geopolitical conditions "continue to shift under the surface," he said, according to JPMorgan's earnings release. These forces may be manageable, he added, but the bank remains prepared for a wide range of outcomes. Also read: JPMorgan CEO sends stern warning on the next credit cycle Washington's borrowing tops the list. The federal government closed fiscal 2026 with a deficit of about $1.99 trillion, which was $217 billion wider than the year before. The debt pile hasn't stopped growing either, reaching roughly $40.39 trillion on Oct. 15. Inflation and interest rates are tangled together. In May, a spike in crude oil sent the Consumer Price Index to 4.2%, its highest reading in three years, CBS News reported. The Fed answered in September by raising rates for the first time since 2023 and hinted that another hike could come this year. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said plainly that inflation had stayed too high for too long. The last two threats are harder to measure. Dimon has pointed to the remilitarization of the world and the restructuring of trade as forces that could raise prices, and inflation has risen during the Iran conflict. On the earnings call, he also acknowledged that times are good, with high asset prices and fairly low credit losses. Elevated valuations leave less room for error if any of the other four threats flare up. On the balance sheet, JPMorgan is padding its cushion. It set aside $2.7 billion for credit losses during the quarter, and $539 million of that went into reserves, mostly for wholesale loans. The bank also pulled back on share buybacks. Actual losses are still in check, though, since net charge-offs came in lower than a year ago. Dimon is also getting pickier about who gets a loan. "We are tightening up a little bit credit," he told analysts, adding that some credit terms have become a little looser. In plain terms, the bank is being more careful about the loans it makes.

JPMorgan Predicts Bitcoin Will Outpace Stocks, Bonds, and Gold Over the Next Decade. Is Bitcoin Now a Screaming Buy?

No summary available

JPMorgan Chase's (NYSE: JPM) asset management division recently released the 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, an annual research report that includes 10- to 15-year return projections. For the first time, it has a returns forecast for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), and expects the top crypt...

JPMorgan Chase's (NYSE: JPM) asset management division recently released the 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, an annual research report that includes 10- to 15-year return projections. For the first time, it has a returns forecast for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), and expects the top cryptocurrency to outperform the major asset classes. It's another sign of the growing acceptance of cryptocurrency. CEO Jamie Dimon previously called Bitcoin a fraud, and as recently as 2025, he said he didn't see its value. However, a positive forecast doesn't necessarily mean Bitcoin is a slam-dunk investment. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » JPMorgan's base case for Bitcoin is 10% annualized returns over the next 10 to 15 years, but the bank sees a wide range of potential returns. Its bear case is -11.2%, and its bull case is about 16.5%. For perspective, JPMorgan forecasts annualized returns of 7.5% for U.S. large-cap stocks, 7.7% for small-cap stocks, 5.5% for gold, and 5.6% to 6.6% for U.S. bonds. Real estate investment trusts (REITs) came in at 8.2%. If JPMorgan's base cases are accurate, $100 invested in Bitcoin would grow to $259 over the next 10 years. The same amount invested in large caps would grow to $206. The press release for JPMorgan's report specifically noted that Bitcoin isn't included as an allocation. The bank also hasn't yet included Bitcoin in its main covariance matrices, the models it uses to determine how much of an asset belongs in a portfolio. JPMorgan laid out two obstacles to Bitcoin portfolio use: volatility and unstable correlations with other assets. Cryptocurrency is known for its volatility, and in Bitcoin's case, JPMorgan assumes 55% annualized volatility, compared to 18% for U.S. large caps and 17.2% for gold. This volatility is why there's such a large gap between the bull and bear cases for Bitcoin. In the bear case, where Bitcoin loses 11.2% per year, you'd end up with roughly 30% of your money after 10 years. Bitcoin's unstable correlations with other assets make it difficult to allocate in a portfolio. You can't count on it as a hedge or to balance out risk, because even though it's sometimes called "digital gold," Bitcoin doesn't perform that way. Gold has held its value during several stock sell-offs, whereas Bitcoin frequently falls with the stock market.

The pool comprises 292 first-lien, fixed-rate residential mortgage loans with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of $340.9 million as of the October 1, 2026 cut-off date. JPMorgan Chase & Co. JPM is advancing its expansion plans in Nigeria after the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) granted approval-in-principle to establish JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited. The move marks a significant step in JPMorgan's efforts to deepen its presence in Africa's largest economy and expand its corporate and institutional banking services. The CBN granted approval-in-principle to JPMorgan on Oct. 23, 2026, allowing it to proceed with plans to establish a merchant bank in Nigeria. The development follows the bank's reported deposit of 50 billion Nigerian naira (approximately $38 million) with CBN as part of its licensing process. The deposit represented a key regulatory requirement but did not guarantee approval. JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited is expected to expand the bank's ability to serve Nigerian corporations and institutional clients. Its proposed activities include wholesale banking, capital markets and advisory services. The expansion could also create opportunities in lending, payments, trade finance and cross-border transactions. JPMorgan has maintained a representative office in Lagos for years. Establishing a locally licensed merchant bank would provide a broader platform to serve businesses and participate in Nigeria's financial markets. The approval-in-principle represents only the initial stage of the regulatory process. JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited must complete the remaining requirements, including incorporation with the Corporate Affairs Commission and the necessary operational arrangements, before receiving authorization to commence business. The proposed Nigerian merchant bank also aligns with JPMorgan's broader efforts to strengthen its African presence and capture corporate and investment banking opportunities across the region. The bank has reinforced its regional investment banking leadership through appointments covering sub-Saharan Africa, Kenya and Ivory Coast, reflecting its focus on expanding client coverage and strengthening relationships with businesses, governments and institutional investors. Nigeria's position as a major African economy could make the proposed bank a valuable addition to JPMorgan's regional operations. However, the scale of the opportunity will depend on regulatory approvals, client demand and the bank's ability to establish profitable operations. In conclusion, JPMorgan's planned entry into Nigeria's merchant banking sector could strengthen its African presence and create new growth opportunities in corporate banking, capital markets, advisory services and cross-border financing. Nigeria's sizable economy and growing demand for institutional financial services offer significant long-term potential. However, the expansion's success will depend on securing final regulatory approval, attracting corporate clients and building profitable operations amid competition and market challenges. While the approval-in-principle marks an important milestone, its contribution to JPMorgan's overall growth will ultimately depend on how effectively the bank converts its expanded presence into sustainable revenue and earnings.

Still, the team pointed to several offsetting positives. The strategists said they do not expect investors to "sustainably re-engage with French exposure" until the main political risks pass, favoring a trade of being overweight non-French domestic exposure versus French exposure "medium term." They also do not expect French risk to spread into broader Europe, noting banks are in much stronger shape than during the euro crisis, credit defaults remain low, and the European Central Bank serves as "a credible backstop this time around." The US company's net revenue rose to $12.1 billion in the three months to September 30, while net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) increased 18% to $6 billion. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 17% to $3.48, while reported earnings per share rose 22% to $3.19, reflecting the impact of one-off charges in the previous year. Payments volume increased 9% on a constant-dollar basis, while cross-border payments rose 14% and processed transactions climbed 10% to 74.2 billion, highlighting continued demand for travel and everyday purchases. Data processing revenue grew 16% to $6.2 billion, while international transaction revenue increased 8% to $4.1 billion, according to Visa's results for the quarter. However, client incentives, payments and other benefits offered to financial institutions and partners, rose 21% to $5.1 billion, as Visa secured new agreements and prepared for further contract renewals. Visa expects incentive growth to accelerate in the 2027 financial year, with about 25% of payments volume due for renewal, compared with 20% in 2026. The company forecast low-double-digit to low-teens growth in adjusted earnings per share and low-double-digit revenue growth for 2027, while higher incentives could weigh on profitability. For the full 2026 financial year, net revenue increased 15% to $45.9 billion and adjusted earnings per share rose 16% to $13.27. Visa also increased its quarterly cash dividend by 16% to $0.78 a share.

The CEO and Co-Founder of StraitsX sits down with JD Durkin at Money 20/20 USA in Las Vegas to share that 85% of the company's stablecoin card transactions are under $50, for everyday purchases like groceries and diapers. Liu explains how the Singapore-based payment infrastructure company, a regulated stablecoin issuer licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, has become one of the world's largest issuers of stablecoin-backed Visa debit cards, processing more than $500 million in card payments every month. He shares how stablecoins give people in emerging markets fast access to US dollars to protect their savings against inflation, and why he wears an NFC payment ring instead of carrying a card. He also predicts that, like the internet before it, stablecoin technology will fade into the background of everyday life.

Both cross-border and processed transactions grew by double-digit percentages. Service revenue increased 14% to $5.26 billion, while data processing sales climbed 16% to $6.25 billion. Visa expects fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to increase by a low-double digit to low-teens percentage figure on a constant-dollar basis. It sees adjusted net revenue rising by a low double digit. Analysts expect non-GAAP EPS of $15.04 for the fiscal year and nearly 11% annual sales growth to $50.83 billion. For the ongoing three-month period, Visa expects adjusted EPS to grow at the low end of mid-teens and net revenue to rise by low-double digits. Wall Street is looking for EPS of $3.62 and nearly 12% year-over-year sales growth to $12.18 billion. Visa shares declined 1.4% in after-hours trading. They have gained 15% this year through Tuesday's close. Rival Mastercard (MA) is scheduled to report its quarterly results Thursday.

Visa employees can receive approved reimbursements on eligible debit cards through Visa Direct instead of waiting for checks or traditional bank transfers BOZEMAN, Mont., October 27, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Payouts Network™ announced today that Visa employees can receive approved U.S. relocation reimbursements on eligible debit cards through the Payouts Network platform and Visa Direct. Employees can receive reimbursement funds quickly after expenses are approved, rather than wait for a check in the mail or a traditional bank transfer. Payouts Network uses Visa Direct, Visa's money movement network, to send approved reimbursements to an employee's eligible debit card. Employees enter their card information on a Payouts Network page instead of sharing bank routing and account numbers for an Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfer. Their card information can be securely stored as a token, making future reimbursements easier. When funds become available depends on the card, the receiving financial institution and other factors. "Relocating for work is a big life change, and employees often have significant expenses before they've even settled into their new homes," said Keith Smith, chief executive officer of Payouts Network. "Once a reimbursement is approved, there's no reason the employee should have to wait days to receive it. We're helping Visa make that experience fast and easy for its people." A work-related move can mean paying upfront for travel, temporary housing, deposits and movers. Employees don't always pay the full amount themselves, but when they cover expenses and wait to be reimbursed, the delay can add pressure to their finances. Relocation reimbursements are one way businesses use Payouts Network. The platform also handles airline service recovery credits, insurance claims, rewards and incentives. With one integration, businesses can send payouts, communicate with recipients, set their own payment rules and track results. About Payouts Network Payouts Network helps businesses make more of every payout. Its configurable digital disbursement platform brings payment delivery, communication, business rules and real-time reporting together to create better experiences for recipients and more control for businesses. The platform supports instant payouts, digital credits, rewards, incentives and reimbursements. Payouts Network is based in Bozeman, Montana. Learn more at payoutsnetwork.com. RESTON, Va., Sept. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today issued a letter to shareholders from Lightbridge's Chairman & Chief Executive Officer, Seth Grae, following the Company's selection for the U.S. Department of Energy's Launch Pad INL Program. Dear Shareholders, Recently, we announced that Lightbridge has been selected to participate in the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) Launch Pad program at Idaho National Laboratory (INL). This is an important milestone for our Company that can enable an accelerated pathway for the commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel™. In this letter, I want to provide additional context on the significance of this milestone and convey why we believe we will look back on this day as one of the most consequential milestones in Lightbridge's history. What makes this milestone so significant for Lightbridge? DOE's Launch Pad INL enables a new two-prong commercialization strategy. The Special HALEU Extrusion Demonstration (SHED) facility that will produce Lead Test Assemblies (LTAs) will be deployed under DOE authorization. The Lightbridge Expandable Fuel Facility (LEFF) will proceed separately toward U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) licensing for commercial-scale production (see below). This two-pronged approach can accelerate our time-to-market by several years compared to our previous projections. While detailed cost estimates for SHED are still being developed, based on preliminary estimates, we currently expect our existing cash and financial resources to be sufficient to fund the construction, operation, and decommissioning of SHED. The path for SHED goes through the DOE. The path for LEFF runs through the NRC. Which one applies depends on the facility's scale and purpose. SHED, a pilot-scale facility that produces LTAs, the full-size assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel that a utility would load into the core of an operating commercial reactor, which the NRC treats as part of a testing program, does not require an NRC license. LEFF, a commercial-scale fuel fabrication facility, does. We've previously described LEFF as the world's first fuel fabrication plant designed to expand in capacity as commercial demand for our fuel grows. Our original plan was to build LEFF under an NRC license in stages, starting with pilot-scale fabrication to produce LTAs, and then expand production to commercial scale to support batch reloads. That path is well understood from a regulatory licensing standpoint but would cost substantially more and take much longer.

Lightbridge Corporation Pays Tribute to Ambassador Thomas Graham Jr., Former Executive Chairman of the Board

RESTON, Va., Sept. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR) was deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ambassador (ret.) Thomas Graham Jr., at the age of 92. He served as Executive Chairman of the Company's Board of Directors from 2009 to 2022 and as Chairman from 2022 to 2024. A defining figure in Lightbridge's history, Ambassador Graham devoted nearly two decades to the Company and brought a career centered on American arms control and nuclear non-proliferation policy. A graduate of Princeton University and Harvard Law School, Ambassador Graham served as a senior U.S. diplomat involved in every major international arms control and non-proliferation negotiation in which the United States participated between 1970 and 1997 — including the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks, the START I and START II Treaties, the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, the Conventional Armed Forces in Europe Treaty, and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty. He spent 15 years as general counsel of the U.S. Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and served as its Acting Director in 1993. Appointed by President Clinton as Special Representative of the President for Arms Control, Non-Proliferation, and Disarmament from 1994 to 1997, he led the U.S. government's effort that secured the permanent extension of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in 1995. Ambassador Graham joined Lightbridge as Executive Chairman in 2009 and helped shape the Company's founding proposition: that advanced nuclear fuel technology could improve the economics and safety of nuclear power while strengthening proliferation resistance. He carried creative thinking relating to non-proliferation well beyond the boardroom — as an appointee to the United Arab Emirates' International Advisory Board on nuclear energy from 2009 to 2016, as co-author of Seeing the Light: The Case for Nuclear Power in the 21st Century, and as Co-Chairman of the Atlantic Council's Nuclear Energy and National Security Coalition. Across fifteen books and more than 100 published articles, he made the case that non-proliferation and the expansion of civil nuclear energy were not competing goals. He was named Chairman Emeritus of Lightbridge in 2024 and retired from the Company the following year. Seth Grae, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge Corporation: "Tom's name on our board did something no business plan could: it told governments, regulators, and investors that a company working on nuclear fuel took non-proliferation seriously as a first principle. He negotiated the treaties that shaped the nuclear order and spent his last two decades arguing that the same seriousness could make nuclear energy larger, not smaller. He asked hard questions at every board meeting I attended with him, and Lightbridge is a better, more credible company for it. On behalf of our Board of Directors and our entire team, I extend our deepest condolences to his family." RESTON, Va., Sept. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the Japan Patent Office ("JPO") for Japanese Patent Application No. 20...

RESTON, Va., Sept. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the Japan Patent Office ("JPO") for Japanese Patent Application No. 2024-513980, titled "Multi-Zone Fuel Element." The allowed claims cover the fuel element design itself, a fuel assembly incorporating that design, and a method of producing the element through additive manufacturing (3D printing), extending protection for a core element of Lightbridge Fuel into a market with one of the world's largest nuclear power markets. The patent covers a fuel rod composed of three layers of different materials, with each layer varying in thickness along the rod's length. That shape can be designed to control how the fuel behaves at different points inside the reactor, improving performance and safety margins. The claims also cover the fuel assembly into which these rods go and the 3D printing method used to build them. Japan has 32 reactors classified as operable, of which 15 have received clearance from the country's Nuclear Regulation Authority and returned to service, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Japan's national energy plan targets nuclear power at approximately 20% of electricity generation by fiscal year 2040, which would require up to 30 reactors in operation. "Japan operates a significant nuclear fleet and has made nuclear power central to its energy security and decarbonization policy, which makes it an important market for us," said Seth Grae, Chairman & CEO of Lightbridge Corporation. "This decision covers the fuel rod and the assembly that holds it, and the additive manufacturing method that produces it. That three-way coverage matters commercially because it protects the fuel product, which a utility will actually load into a reactor, and the process we intend to use to produce it." Lightbridge's fuel technology is backed by an extensive worldwide patent portfolio spanning jurisdictions representing the majority of global nuclear generating capacity. About Lightbridge Corporation Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR) is focused on developing advanced nuclear fuel technology essential to delivering abundant, zero-emission, clean energy and providing energy security to the world. The Company is developing Lightbridge Fuel™, a proprietary next-generation nuclear fuel technology for existing light-water and pressurized heavy-water reactors, significantly enhancing reactor safety, economics, and proliferation resistance. The Company is also developing Lightbridge Fuel for new small modular reactors to deliver the same benefits, when combined with load-following with renewables, on a zero-carbon electric grid.

Provides an Accelerated Pathway toward DOE Authorization to Manufacture Lead Test Assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel for Operation in Commercial Power Reactors RESTON, Va., Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fue...

Provides an Accelerated Pathway toward DOE Authorization to Manufacture Lead Test Assemblies of Lightbridge Fuel for Operation in Commercial Power Reactors RESTON, Va., Aug. 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that it has been selected to participate in the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad INL, administered by the U.S. Department of Energy's ("DOE") National Reactor Innovation Center ("NRIC") at Idaho National Laboratory ("INL"). Selection provides an accelerated pathway toward DOE authorization for Lightbridge to design, build, and operate a dedicated facility at INL to manufacture Lead Test Assemblies ("LTAs") of Lightbridge Fuel — the Company's proprietary metallic nuclear fuel — for testing in U.S. commercial power reactors. LTAs represent the final fuel qualification stage between reactor testing and commercial fuel sales. Lightbridge now has an accelerated pathway to establishing manufacturing capability for producing LTAs. The selection marks the most significant advance to date in Lightbridge's path from fuel testing to commercial deployment. By establishing a dedicated manufacturing facility under DOE authorization, the Company expects to significantly shorten the timeline for producing LTAs for operation in a commercial U.S. reactor. "This is the most important step we have taken toward putting Lightbridge Fuel into commercial reactors, and it changes how investors should understand our timeline," said Seth Grae, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge. "A DOE-authorized facility will let us manufacture full-scale Lightbridge Fuel assemblies that nuclear utilities will run in their plants, and can produce them years sooner than a conventional facility licensing path would allow. We have been working with a major engineering, procurement, and construction ("EPC") firm in preparation for the start of construction of the Special High-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) Extrusion Demonstration (SHED) facility as soon as next year. Our goal is for Lightbridge Fuel to become the standard fuel that produces most of the world's nuclear energy, and this is where that path begins." Launch Pad is a DOE initiative supporting the Trump administration's goal of widescale nuclear energy expansion through streamlined pathways for developers to demonstrate and accelerate commercial deployment. Facilities developed under the program are privately financed. Lightbridge continues to develop detailed cost estimates for SHED, and based on preliminary estimates, the anticipated cost to construct, operate, and decommission SHED can be funded from the Company's current cash and financial resources.

RESTON, Va., Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, announced its financial results for the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2026, and provided an update on the Company's continued progress. Seth Grae, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge, commented, "In the first half of 2026, our fuel development work at Idaho National Laboratory produced its first irradiated material for examination. In May, the first batch of our fuel material samples was removed from the Advanced Test Reactor with members of our engineering team and senior management present. Those samples are now cooling ahead of post-irradiation examination (PIE), which we expect to begin later this year. The PIE will produce our first material property data under high burn-up conditions, while irradiation of the remaining samples continues. We also received notices of allowance from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office covering our multi-lobed fuel assembly for pressurized heavy water reactors, and from the European Patent Office covering our multi-zone fuel element and its additive manufacturing method across 39 contracting states." "In May, we partnered with Studsvik Scandpower to develop an extension of the Studsvik CMS5 Core Management Suite to model the new Lightbridge Fuel™ design, placing our design inside the state-of-the-art software that utilities already rely on worldwide. Then in June, I represented Lightbridge at the White House launch of UPRISE, the Department of Energy initiative targeting approximately 5 GW of end capacity drawn from reactors already operating. As electricity demand accelerates, driven by AI and hyperscale data centers, the fastest and least expensive additional nuclear-generated megawatts will come from increasing the power output of currently operating reactors. Lightbridge Fuel is being designed to deliver the largest power uprates available while enhancing safety and operating at approximately 1,000°C cooler than conventional fuel." "Since the quarter end, we signed a memorandum of understanding with Quadrant Nuclear Industries to establish a framework for long-term HALEU supply from its planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory. Securing domestic fuel supply is work that has to be done years before the fuel is needed, and we intend to be early rather than late. Lightbridge was also added to the Solactive Global Uranium & Nuclear Components Total Return Index, the benchmark that is tracked by the Global X Uranium ETF, beginning earlier this week. As with the Russell indexes, joining this prestigious index broadens the base of investors with ownership of our stock."

Companies to explore long-term HALEU supply arrangements supporting the commercialization of next-generation nuclear fuel technologies RESTON, Va. and BOSTON, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation (Nasdaq: LTBR), a leader in advanced nuclear fuel technology, and Quadrant Nuclear Industries Inc. (QNI), a developer of integrated nuclear fuel cycle capabilities, today announced they have entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to establish a framework for collaboration on the long-term supply of high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel. The MoU reflects a shared commitment to strengthening the domestic nuclear fuel supply chain, advancing next-generation nuclear technologies, and supporting U.S. energy security and decarbonization objectives. Under the agreement, Lightbridge and QNI will engage in discussions regarding the potential supply and long-term offtake of HALEU produced at QNI's planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory. "We are pleased to establish this Memorandum of Understanding with QNI as we continue advancing the commercialization of Lightbridge Fuel™," said Seth Grae, Chairman and CEO of Lightbridge Corporation. "As we progress in the development and regulatory licensing of Lightbridge Fuel™, it is critical that we begin solidifying a reliable domestic supply of HALEU. We look forward to working with QNI to explore opportunities that support our long-term fuel requirements and contribute to a more secure U.S. nuclear fuel supply chain." "Developing a secure, U.S.-based source of HALEU is essential to enabling the next generation of nuclear energy," said Dee Mewbourne, CEO of QNI. "Our cooperation with Lightbridge reflects the growing alignment between advanced fuel innovation and domestic fuel production. Through this collaboration, we aim to establish a framework for a long-term offtake arrangement that supports commercialization of Lightbridge's advanced fuel technology while strengthening the domestic nuclear fuel ecosystem." QNI is developing an integrated HALEU production capability in coordination with the U.S. Department of Energy and other key stakeholders. Its planned Vanguard facility at Idaho National Laboratory is designed to produce up to eighteen metric tons of HALEU annually at full capacity, supporting both commercial and government markets for advanced nuclear reactors. The companies intend to collaborate on areas including fuel supply planning, technical interface requirements, commercial structuring, regulatory coordination, and logistics considerations associated with HALEU supply arrangements.

RESTON, Va., June 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that the first batch of its fuel material samples undergoing irradiation at the Idaho National Laboratory's (INL) Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) have been successfully removed and will now be cooled down over the next several months in preparation for post-irradiation examination, which is expected to begin later this year. The samples were removed on May 6, 2026, with Lightbridge's full-time fuel engineering team and senior management — 24 Lightbridge personnel in total — on site at INL for the milestone. On May 7, the Lightbridge team met with the INL personnel leading the project, including John Wagner, Laboratory Director of Idaho National Laboratory, and Jess Gehin, Associate Lab Director. Lightbridge discussed progress to date and the path forward across multiple Lightbridge projects currently underway at INL. "The data already developed at the Advanced Test Reactor is a meaningful validation of the innovation and engineering behind Lightbridge Fuel," said Seth Grae, President and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge. "The data to be collected during the planned post-irradiation examination are expected to support our ongoing fuel performance modeling activities and regulatory licensing efforts for commercial deployment of Lightbridge Fuel. We are grateful to Lab Director John Wagner, Associate Lab Director Jess Gehin, and the entire INL team for the operational excellence that has made this campaign possible." Image 1: The combined Lightbridge and Idaho National Laboratory Team (May 7, 2026) The fuel material samples are being tested under the Fission Accelerated Steady-state Testing (FAST) method, an accelerated irradiation technique that uses Highly Enriched Uranium to reach high burnup conditions faster than conventional test methods. The FAST method was conceived and developed at INL. Geoffrey "Boone" Beausoleil, Lightbridge's Director of Materials, played a key role on the INL team that originated the initial concept for FAST and developed the underlying testing methodology during his prior tenure at INL. Image 2: Several members of Lightbridge team looking over the ATR canal (May 6, 2026) The samples that have been removed from the ATR will undergo post-irradiation examination to collect the data on fundamental material properties under high-burnup irradiation conditions. The data developed will support the broader testing program aimed at confirming the safety, performance, and economic advantages of Lightbridge Fuel relative to conventional nuclear fuel used in commercial reactors worldwide.

Together, Lightbridge and Studsvik will provide the commercial nuclear sector with a software package for light water reactors (LWRs) that is fully supported by the state-of-the-art Studsvik software already adopted by customers around the world. Lightbridge is developing a next-generation nuclear fuel design, Lightbridge Fuel, to improve the economics, safety, and proliferation resistance of existing and new reactors. The design includes metallic fuel rods that will be more economical and safer than traditional fuel. "As we advance our efforts to license Lightbridge Fuel for use in commercial nuclear power plants, we are pleased to leverage Studsvik's CMS5 software to help drive these initiatives forward," said Seth Grae, President and CEO of Lightbridge. "We are pleased to partner with Lightbridge as they take this important step in advancing the licensing of their next-generation fuel product," said Art Wharton, President of the Studsvik Scandpower Group. "Studsvik Scandpower remains committed to continuously enhancing our software capabilities to support the nuclear industry's growth and the development of innovative fuel technologies." This partnership further strengthens Lightbridge and Studsvik's position in the global nuclear industry. About Studsvik Studsvik provides a range of advanced technical services to the global nuclear power industry. Our core areas of expertise include fuel and materials technology, software for core monitoring and fuel optimisation, decommissioning and radiation protection services, as well as technical solutions for the handling, conditioning, and volume reduction of radioactive waste. The company has over 75 years of experience in nuclear technology and services in radiological environments. Studsvik employs approximately 540 people across 7 countries and is listed on the Nasdaq Stockholm. About Lightbridge Corporation Lightbridge Corporation (NASDAQ: LTBR) is focused on developing advanced nuclear fuel technology essential to delivering abundant, zero-emission, clean energy and providing energy security to the world. The Company is developing Lightbridge Fuel™, a proprietary next-generation nuclear fuel technology for existing light-water and pressurized heavy-water reactors, significantly enhancing reactor safety, economics, and proliferation resistance. The Company is also developing Lightbridge Fuel for new small modular reactors to deliver the same benefits, plus load-following with renewables, on a zero-carbon electric grid.

Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But the harsh reality is that very many loss making companies burn through all their cash and go bankrupt. So should Lightbridge (NASDAQ:LTBR) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). Let's start with an examination of the business' cash, relative to its cash burn. We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free. You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. As at March 2026, Lightbridge had cash of US$216m and no debt. In the last year, its cash burn was US$16m. That means it had a cash runway of very many years as of March 2026. Even though this is but one measure of the company's cash burn, the thought of such a long cash runway warms our bellies in a comforting way. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years. View our latest analysis for Lightbridge Lightbridge didn't record any revenue over the last year, indicating that it's an early stage company still developing its business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. With the cash burn rate up 44% in the last year, it seems that the company is ratcheting up investment in the business over time. However, the company's true cash runway will therefore be shorter than suggested above, if spending continues to increase. Lightbridge makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. So we'd generally prefer stocks from this list of stocks that have analysts forecasting growth. Given its cash burn trajectory, Lightbridge shareholders may wish to consider how easily it could raise more cash, despite its solid cash runway. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By looking at a company's cash burn relative to its market capitalisation, we gain insight on how much shareholders would be diluted if the company needed to raise enough cash to cover another year's cash burn.

RESTON, Va., April 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, announced its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, and provided an update on the Company's continued progress. Seth Grae, President & Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge, commented, "The first quarter of 2026 reflects the depth and pace of Lightbridge's program execution. We received patent allowances from three major jurisdictions—Canada, the United States, and the European Patent Office—expanding the scope of patent protection for Lightbridge Fuel™ across the CANDU fleet, the U.S. domestic light water reactor market, and 39 European contracting states. We also entered into an engineering contract with Stern Laboratories to launch a multi-phase thermal-hydraulics test program to support U.S. regulatory licensing of our fuel for light water reactors. We were selected to serve on the Industry Advisory Board of a $6 million DOE-funded research initiative at Penn State. And our technical team presented proprietary uranium-zirconium alloy research at TMS2026, contributing to the scientific foundation that underpins everything we are building." "We believe this is the most promising time for the growth of nuclear power in decades. Record global generation in 2025, sweeping U.S. executive action to accelerate reactor permitting and NRC reform, and landmark procurement commitments from the world's largest technology companies have collectively shifted the industry from a question of 'if' to a question of 'when and how fast.' Lightbridge is building to be the answer to the 'how'—specifically, how the existing global reactor fleet and new-build water-cooled reactors deliver more power and further enhanced safety, with improved economics." "Our program is advancing on every front. We have grown to over two dozen in-house engineers across all of our core disciplines, including neutronics, thermal hydraulics, fuel performance, materials, fuel assembly mechanical design, licensing, high-performance computing, and program management, and we continue to add talent. The qualification pathway ahead of us is well-defined. We expect Lightbridge Fuel will enable power uprates of up to 30% or more for new-build water-cooled reactors, meaningfully more than any other approach, while operating approximately 1,000 degrees Celsius cooler. In existing light-water reactors, Lightbridge Fuel is expected to enable power uprates of up to 20% or more (depending on balance-of-plant constraints) and to extend the fuel cycle length. In addition to creating new nuclear generating capacity, the world is seeking greater power from the infrastructure it already has. That is precisely the problem we've designed Lightbridge Fuel to solve."

Lightbridge Receives Notice of Allowance for European Patent Covering Multi-Zone Fuel Element and Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) Method

No summary available

RESTON, Va., April 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that the European Patent Office (EPO) has issued a Notice of Allowance for European Patent Application No. 22777419.7,...

RESTON, Va., April 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Lightbridge Corporation ("Lightbridge" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: LTBR), an advanced nuclear fuel technology company, today announced that the European Patent Office (EPO) has issued a Notice of Allowance for European Patent Application No. 22777419.7, titled "Multi-Zone Fuel Element." The allowed patent covers Lightbridge's proprietary nuclear fuel element design, featuring multiple radial zones with variable thicknesses along the axial direction, enabling precise control of neutron flux distribution throughout the fuel element's operational lifetime. The European allowance extends intellectual property protection for a core element of Lightbridge's fuel technology across 39 contracting states, including the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and all major European nuclear markets. The patent covers fuel elements manufactured via additive manufacturing (3D printing), a process that enables the production of complex multi-material zone architectures that are unachievable through conventional fuel fabrication techniques. Combined with Lightbridge's existing U.S. and international patent portfolio, this grant meaningfully expands the Company's IP moat in advanced nuclear fuel. The allowed claims are directed to a fuel element comprising three distinct radial zones of different materials — a first zone extending along the central axis, a second surrounding zone, and a third outermost zone — in which the thickness of both the second and third zones in the radial direction varies along the axial direction. The manufacturing method claims cover the use of additive manufacturing to produce this multi-zone architecture using metallic, ceramic, or cermet fuel systems. The variable zone thickness along the axial direction enables engineers to tailor the radial and axial neutron flux profile within a single element, supporting optimization of reactor performance, safety margin management, and fissile material efficiency throughout the fuel cycle. "Receiving this allowance from the European Patent Office is an important validation of the technical depth and novelty of Lightbridge Fuel™," said Seth Grae, President and Chief Executive Officer of Lightbridge Corporation. "Europe is home to a significant installed base of nuclear generating capacity, and the countries and utilities advancing nuclear energy as part of their clean energy programs represent a natural market for Lightbridge Fuel. This patent ensures that the fuel element design at the heart of Lightbridge Fuel, with our precise multi-zone architecture and variable radial zone configuration, is protected across those markets as we advance toward commercialization."

The index's 25 worst performers fell an average of 42.4% in the first half, according to Bespoke Investment Group data cited by Seeking Alpha. Since July, they've rebounded 34.6%. Bespoke described the group as a mix of consumer stocks and software names that investors expected AI to make obsolete. Yet the group is still down about 22% for the year. Nvidia forges supplier agreements to expand capacity for AI

No summary available

This story was originally published on Supply Chain Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Supply Chain Dive newsletter. Nvidia unveiled agreements with a half-dozen suppliers to increase capacity to meet high demand for artificial intelligence systems powered by the ...

This story was originally published on Supply Chain Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Supply Chain Dive newsletter. Nvidia unveiled agreements with a half-dozen suppliers to increase capacity to meet high demand for artificial intelligence systems powered by the company's chips, according to an Oct. 21 press release. Nvidia inked agreements with Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corp. to increase manufacturing capacity 2.5 times in aggregate over three years. The chipmaker also unveiled capacity agreements with partners Amkor Technology, King Yuan Electronics Co. and Siliconware Precision Industries to support production of systems that train and run AI models. "We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history," Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and CEO, said in the release. "Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint." Ibiden, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron make substrates — specialized circuit boards that connect Nvidia's processors to a computer's main circuit board. Samsung Electro-Mechanics will upgrade facilities and build new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, the company will allocate "a significant portion" of its total annual package substrate production capacity to Nvidia, per the release. Unimicron's agreement with Nvidia covers a manufacturing expansion in Taiwan scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028, according to the release. Nvidia is providing Ibiden with a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation for a plant expansion in Japan, the release says. The deal, signed earlier this year, aims to triple the plant's current capacity. Ibiden expects additional production to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Under Nvidia's agreement with Amkor, the packaging company plans to expand capacity at its South Korea plants to assemble chips into connected units, a process called advanced packaging. Specifically, Amkor has agreed to increase its capacity to process interposer-containing wafers by 300% by the end of 2028. An interposer is a connecting layer that allows communication between separate chips in the same package. With KYEC, Nvidia has provided $1.1 billion to support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment. High-volume production is expected to start in April 2027. Siliconware Precision Industries plans to work with Nvidia to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan 15-fold by mid-2027, while targeting another doubling of capacity by the end of 2028. The expansion will support advanced optical engines that provide the bandwidth and power-efficiency requirements of AI systems.

For investors, this presents a compelling opportunity to gain exposure not only to Meta but also to the broader group of technology giants, including Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, which are increasingly interconnected through capital investments and hardware dependencies within the AI ecosystem. Against this backdrop, rather than betting on a single winner in this complex web, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with these tech behemoths in their top holdings offer investors a diversified vehicle to capture the collective upside of these billion-dollar investments. Before identifying specific funds, it is important to understand how these investments could benefit the broader AI industry and why diversified ETF exposure may offer advantages over picking individual stocks, as discussed below. The investment commitments, like those recently made by NVDA and AMD, are not merely financial maneuvers; they are strategic moves to lock in the hardware ecosystem and stave off threats from custom silicon. By investing in Meta, Nvidia and AMD secure a massive customer for their high-margin AI accelerators. Meta, in turn, secures prioritized access to essential compute power to scale its rapidly growing Muse AI agent, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure and AMD's EPYC processors. This creates a feedback loop: Meta's AI success drives demand for chips, which funds further chip innovation, benefiting the entire supply chain within the AI ecosystem. This is, in fact, part of a broader trend in 2026 where tech giants are vertically integrating via capital injection. Nvidia has aggressively invested in the AI ecosystem, participating in 121 funding rounds this year, a massive jump from just 13 in 2022. Similarly, AMD recently committed up to $5 billion to Anthropic. Furthermore, interest from Broadcom, an already established critical custom-chip partner of Meta, in Meta's latest equity offering highlights that the AI infrastructure buildout is a multi-vendor race requiring immense capital.

In 1997, with his company Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) mere weeks away from hitting insolvency, Jensen Huang ordered mass production of a graphics chip that had never physically existed — betting his company's last dollars on a design tested entirely inside a simulator. The chip was the RIVA 128 and Huang called that decision, made when Nvidia had "about six months of cash left," as the defining moment that saved the company. Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change Gold has overtaken U.S. Treasuries as central banks' top reserve asset. Get Goldco's 2026 Precious Metals IRA Playbook for free Huang recalled the pivotal and harrowing events during an episode of the Acquired podcast (1), recorded at Nvidia's headquarters and published back in October 2023. At the time of that recording, Nvidia was worth about $1.1 trillion. Today, it's worth around $5.3 trillion (2), making it the most valuable public company on earth — a position it reached after becoming the first company ever to top a $5 trillion valuation (3) in October 2025. Considering Nvidia's wild success, it's easy to forget that it was all built on a gamble, or perhaps a wish and a prayer. To understand the risk, you have to understand what "taping out" a chip means. In semiconductor design, taping out is essentially the point of no return: It's the moment a company sends its finished blueprint to a factory to be manufactured, or "fabricated." Fixing a mistake after that means starting a fresh production run, which costs money and months most startups truly don't have. The normal process, Huang explained, is iterative: You build the chip, write the software, find and stamp out any bugs, then tape out a corrected version. Repeat as needed. But 30 years ago, Nvidia couldn't afford to repeat anything. "If we only had six months and you get to tape out just one time, then obviously you're going to tape out a perfect chip," Huang said. Huang had a darkly hilarious answer when his engineers asked how he could possibly know the chip would be perfect: "I know it's going to be perfect because if it's not we'll be out of business. So let's make it perfect." The workaround was emulation.

Anduril, Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a new kind of US-made laptop

No summary available

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. And by that, he doesn't just mean assembly, but the production of every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today. Anduril is partnering with Qualcomm to achieve that mission with ...

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is vowing to bring computer manufacturing back to the U.S. And by that, he doesn't just mean assembly, but the production of every individual component, some of which are exclusively made in China today. Anduril is partnering with Qualcomm to achieve that mission with a new computer called BlueChip, the companies announced Tuesday. BlueChip will be available for preorder in 2027. While technical details are scant — Anduril hasn't even finished contracting with all its component suppliers yet, according to Luckey — this first product will be a hardened laptop. It will be designed to withstand the most grueling physical environments and meet the security-conscious needs of the military, government, first responders, and law enforcement. For the first generation, about 90% of its components will be made in the U.S. or in allied countries, Anduril says, most notably its CPU. BlueChip will run on a Snapdragon X Series built at TSMC's massive new facility in Arizona. The CPU uses the same architecture that powers other laptops, including the Microsoft Surface, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said during the press conference. "As of right now, the laptop's bill of materials is about 90% U.S. and allied [ally countries], and we have a technical roadmap to get to 100% domestic over time," Luckey said. "The intent in the long run is to have an option that is made entirely in the United States, 100% domestic. And I mean everything. I mean the displays. I mean the metallics. I mean the the magnetics. All of it." Right now, for instance, Luckey says he's found an American supplier for the glass that covers the display, but the display itself is one of several components he says are only manufactured in China. While Luckey says consumers are welcome to order a BlueChip — the company may even create a waiting list for interested consumers — this first PC won't be designed for them. For one thing, as a hardened computer, it will be heavy and have battery-life constraints because of the engineering required to withstand rain, dust, and other rugged conditions. The bigger point is to offer U.S. government agencies a product that complies with regulations requiring them to buy U.S.-made computers. In this case, the selling point is a transparent supply chain that customers can track and audit. "These computers are the anti-surveillance computer. You fully control it," Luckey described in a recent interview. "You know everything that is in it, every single component, and you know every software component that is running on it."

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision. Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings. Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. IonQ shares rose 7% today, Rigetti rose 8% and D-Wave rose about 4%, after Intel agreed to buy quantum software company Classiq in a deal reportedly worth about $2.3 billion. A major chipmaker paying that much for quantum software is a vote of confidence in the sector, and IonQ's selloff over the past month looks overdone. IonQ fell 24% in a month amid a broader quantum selloff and worries about new shares, and its share count has nearly doubled since the end of 2024. IonQ reports third-quarter results on Nov. 5, its first quarter with SkyWater included, and Wall Street expects 254% revenue growth. IonQ (IONQ:NYSE) is up 7% today after Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) agreed to buy quantum software company Classiq, a deal Bloomberg reported is worth about $2.3 billion. The rest of the group came along for the ride: Rigetti Computing (RGTI:NASDAQ) rose 8%, and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS:NASDAQ) gained about 4%. Intel announced the deal after Monday's close and didn't give a price. In its announcement, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Classiq "transforms Intel's Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business." That's a big check for software alone. And Classiq's code runs on all kinds of quantum hardware, including trapped-ion machines like the ones IonQ builds. The timing helps IonQ, too. The stock had dropped 24% in a month as quantum stocks sold off broadly and investors worried about dilution from its $2 billion stock sale and its all-stock Elisity deal, worth up to $1.3 billion. The dilution is real. IonQ's diluted share count roughly doubled from 2021 to 2025: And 429 million shares were outstanding as of Oct. 23, before a single Elisity share has been issued. IonQ ended Monday at 19x forward sales. Its three-year average is 75x, and it peaked at 215x in October 2025: Part of that drop is the revenue mix, though. Forward sales now include SkyWater's foundry revenue, which BofA valued at just 2x sales in September. See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on IonQ, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See IonQ's Analyst Ratings IonQ calls itself "the world's leading full-stack quantum platform and foundry." Now Intel is building the same thing, with far deeper pockets. That's a vote for IonQ's strategy, even if Intel's deal won't close until the first half of 2027.

Intel, Oracle, IBM Join Objections to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue, Bringing Total to 26

No summary available

The tech sector's resistance to tokenized stocks keeps building. Intel, Oracle, IBM, and quantum computing firm IonQ are the latest companies to object to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice from the venue dated Monday. The planned platform, a 50-50 join...

The tech sector's resistance to tokenized stocks keeps building. Intel, Oracle, IBM, and quantum computing firm IonQ are the latest companies to object to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice from the venue dated Monday. The planned platform, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, now lists 26 objecting issuers. That's up from 22 in its Oct. 23 notice, which added Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Marvell. The tally stood at 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15, when the first batch included Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group. In less than two weeks, the list has nearly tripled. Technology companies dominate the roster. Microsoft, Alphabet, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Arm, Cisco, and now Intel and Oracle have all objected, along with banks Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo. IBM and IonQ add two quantum computing players. As before, the notices don't explain the companies' reasons or what an objection means for whether a stock can trade on the platform. OKXICE TSV plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC. Users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable "soulbound" token to trade. The venue is set to operate under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. The latest notice highlights a key risk for investors. Each token represents a claim on a real share held by a third-party "tokenizer" through a registered broker-dealer. If that broker-dealer failed, the notice says, it's uncertain whether tokenized shares in a self-custodied wallet would count as customer property or be covered by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, which protects brokerage customers when firms fail. Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks The notice also says trades must be fully funded, with no margin or borrowing. Liquidity providers don't have to be registered market makers and can pull their liquidity at any time. OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling plans for the venue this month.

Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) is expected to beat third-quarter revenue and earnings forecasts, according to Wedbush, but the broker said the chipmaker's fourth-quarter outlook and guidance on 2027 growth and capital spending will be more important in determining how its shares perform. The broker maintained its 'neutral' rating and $98 price target, saying Intel's shares had fallen about 32% over the past month, creating a more balanced investment outlook. Wedbush expects third-quarter revenue of $16.3 billion, in line with Intel's guidance midpoint and broadly matching analysts' consensus, with non-GAAP earnings of $0.38 a share and gross margins of 42%. The broker said improving server supply late in the quarter could support results, although weaker personal computer demand and rising memory and substrate costs could limit the scale of any earnings beat. Research firm IDC estimated that PC shipments fell about 20% year on year and 9% sequentially during the quarter, creating pressure on Intel's client computing business. Wedbush forecasts fourth-quarter revenue of $17.5 billion, up 7% sequentially, compared with the $16.9 billion consensus estimate, while projecting earnings of $0.49 a share against analysts' forecast of $0.43. The broker expects gross margins to improve to 44% in the fourth quarter as a shift towards server products supports profitability, making management's guidance a key focus for investors. Wedbush also highlighted the potential impact of Intel's August equity issuance, which raised capital through about 242 million shares at $95 each, increasing its estimated weighted share count by about 2% in the third quarter and 5% in the fourth. The broker said investors would look for additional guidance on 2027 expectations, including capital expenditure, as they assess whether Intel's recovery can be sustained. Wedbush's $98 price target is based on about 45 times its forecast 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $2.22 a share, less estimated net debt of $2.37 a share.

Intel and Oracle Plan Expanded Collaboration to Support Enterprise and Agentic AI on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

No summary available

LAS VEGAS, October 27, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ORACLE AI WORLD -- Intel and Oracle today announced plans for a multiyear collaboration intended to expand Intel® Xeon®-based computing on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The collaboration is intended to meet the growing demand for enterprise applicat...

LAS VEGAS, October 27, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ORACLE AI WORLD -- Intel and Oracle today announced plans for a multiyear collaboration intended to expand Intel® Xeon®-based computing on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The collaboration is intended to meet the growing demand for enterprise applications, agentic AI, and inference, and is expected to span current and future Xeon platforms, including planned OCI X14 offerings based on Intel's next-generation server processor codenamed Diamond Rapids. As more enterprises deploy AI agents at scale, CPUs are becoming increasingly critical for executing applications, managing data movement, orchestrating agentic actions and supporting inference across existing business systems. The expanded collaboration between Intel and Oracle is intended to support additional capacity and planned processor capabilities as customers extend existing enterprise systems with AI, while retaining familiar software environments and operational tooling. "As AI agents scale, they need processors that can run software, move and secure data, and accelerate inference. Xeon brings together performance and hardware-based confidential computing, giving organizations a trusted, cost-effective foundation for AI at scale," said Kevork Kechichian, executive vice president and general manager, Intel Data Center Group. "Our expanded collaboration with Oracle is intended to combine Intel's multigenerational roadmap with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's technology to help customers put AI to work faster and more cost-effectively." Building on their decades-long relationship, Intel and Oracle intend to coordinate roadmaps and processor capacity planning to support OCI's expansion. Planned Diamond Rapids-based OCI X14 offerings are expected to bring advances in both AI acceleration and general-purpose computing, including enhanced Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) with FP8, FP16, and BF16 support for optimized inference software, and Intel Advanced Performance Extensions (APX) to help optimized applications execute with less instruction overhead. Together, these innovations are expected to help organizations integrate AI into existing enterprise environments, with capabilities that support embedding generation, reranking, and smaller-model inference alongside the application services and tools AI agents use. "Enterprise AI depends on the applications, data, and tools that let an agent complete useful work," said Pradeep Vincent, executive vice president, compute and AI infrastructure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle. "Our expanded collaboration with Intel is intended to help us grow the compute capacity behind those workloads and support plans to bring enhanced Xeon capabilities to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure through X14. Customers are expected to gain a path to build and scale AI using the enterprise software environments they already rely on."

Intel to acquire Classiq to build full-stack quantum computing platform

No summary available

Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) has agreed to acquire Classiq, a quantum computing software company, in a deal aimed at combining its silicon-based quantum hardware with software that simplifies the development of quantum applications. Bloomberg reports the cost of acquisition as about $2.3 bil...

Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) has agreed to acquire Classiq, a quantum computing software company, in a deal aimed at combining its silicon-based quantum hardware with software that simplifies the development of quantum applications. Bloomberg reports the cost of acquisition as about $2.3 billion. The proposed acquisition would bring Classiq's automated quantum algorithm synthesis platform together with Intel's silicon spin-qubit technology, semiconductor manufacturing expertise and existing quantum software capabilities. Intel said the combination would create a full-stack quantum computing platform designed to make the technology more accessible to developers, researchers and businesses, helping it progress towards mainstream commercial use. Classiq's software allows users to develop quantum applications without needing deep expertise in quantum circuit design, while its platform can operate across different types of quantum hardware rather than being tied to a single technology. Intel has invested in quantum computing since 2015 and said it can manufacture qubit chips and complex cryogenic control electronics at scale using equipment and processes employed in conventional silicon semiconductor production. The acquisition would expand Intel's computing portfolio, which includes central processing units, graphics processing units and application-specific integrated circuits, to include quantum processing units. "This transforms Intel's Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business," said Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan, adding that the deal would build on the company's progress in developing scalable silicon spin-qubit technology. Classiq co-founder and chief executive Nir Minerbi said the companies could accelerate quantum computing adoption by making it easier to create scalable applications. Intel said it intended to continue supporting Classiq's existing integrations with multiple hardware platforms after the transaction, maintaining an open software ecosystem that does not depend on a particular quantum technology. The companies will continue operating independently until the deal closes, with completion expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. Shares of Intel were up around 2.4% on Tuesday morning.

In the to-be-reported quarter, the company is likely to have recorded slightly higher revenues from the Client Computing Group (CCG) segment despite high customer inventory levels and a conservative approach toward placing orders for high-value items. CCG is the company's largest segment and accounts for the lion's share of total revenues. It includes computer CPUs, several server boards, form factor systems and graphic products. During the quarter, Intel expanded its multi-year collaboration with Alphabet Inc.'s Google Cloud. The partnership will help Intel integrate generative AI and cloud technologies across its global operations to support innovation and business growth. Under the agreement, Intel will deploy Gemini Enterprise across its workforce, enabling employees to automate tasks and enhance workflows across engineering, supply chain and corporate operations. Through this collaboration, Intel aims to strengthen its position in AI-driven enterprise and semiconductor innovation. The company will also utilize the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to create custom AI tools for different business functions. In addition, Intel is exploring AI solutions to improve marketing and communications by generating targeted content, identifying relevant subject-matter experts and preparing executive materials more efficiently. These developments are likely to have supported the CCG segment's top line during the quarter. Intel also extended its Core Ultra platform to new Googlebook laptops powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors. The latest processors deliver responsive performance and power efficiency for modern computing. Built on Intel's advanced 18A process technology, the Core Ultra Series 3 integrates CPU, GPU and NPU architectures to support demanding workloads and AI-enabled experiences. The platform is designed to help users multitask across applications while maintaining efficient power consumption for longer battery life. The company has also added enhanced connectivity features to the new Googlebook laptops, including Intel Wi-Fi 7, Dual Intel Bluetooth 6.0 and Intel Thunderbolt. These technologies deliver fast and reliable connections across different environments while supporting seamless device experiences. However, Intel has been facing challenges due to the disruptive rise of over-the-top service providers in this dynamic industry. Price-sensitive competition for customer retention in the core business is expected to intensify in the coming days. Aggressive competition is likely to limit the ability to attract and retain customers and affect operating and financial results. Moreover, high raw material prices due to Middle East tensions, the prolonged Russia-Ukraine war and the consequent economic sanctions against the Putin regime have affected the operation schedules of various firms, affecting Intel's demand schedule. High technological obsolescence of most products has further escalated operating costs.
